description:
A simulated Decibel exchange on recorded Decibel prices (every minute) and order books
        (20 levels, a snapshot about every 10 minutes since 15 Nov 2026 16:00 UTC): test a bot's
        order logic without keys or money. Nothing is sent to Decibel. No registration.
        Taker orders consume the recorded levels: what one order takes is gone for the next (same
        step, TP/SL, margin calls) until the next recorded snapshot; beyond the last level
        nothing fills (IOC/market: partial fill, rest cancelled with the reason). The book is
        moved with the mark only when that is worse for the taker (a buy never pays less than
        mark + half the recorded spread), sizes as recorded. With no book recorded at that time
        (before 15 Nov 2026 16:00 UTC): a synthetic book from the market's median recorded book,
        consumed level by level (mark_capped). A post-only order is checked on the next step
        against the book a taker meets (recorded or synthetic): cancelled only if a buy is at or
        above its best ask (a sell at or below its best bid). Resting limits fill only up to the
        volume traded through their price: recorded trades, or before them the 1-minute candles
        (volume x the share of the candle's range past the price); with neither, they don't fill.
        The clock stops where prices and every market's trades are recorded (a few minutes behind
        now). Each fill says what priced it in priced_by: book, book_shifted, mark_capped, trades
        or candle, and has a fill_id. "fills" (since: ms, limit: up to 500, after_fill_id: the
        previous page's cursor) pages through the fill history; step already returns every fill
        of that step in events.
        action="start" (start_hours_ago: where the clock begins, counted back from the end of the
        recorded data, default 6, at most 336; 30 new sessions an hour and 150 a day per IP;
        maker_fill "through" = a resting limit fills only when the price goes through it,
        default, or "touch") returns a session_id to pass to every other action. Then: "place"
        (market e.g. "BTC", side buy|sell, size, price, time_in_force gtc|post_only|ioc|market,
        reduce_only, client_order_id), "cancel" (order_id), "order" (order_id or client_order_id:
        status and Decibel's cancellation reason), "set_leverage" (market, leverage),
        "set_margin_mode" (market, margin_mode cross|isolated), "add_margin" (market, amount:
        isolated only), "set_tpsl" (market, take_profit, stop_loss: needs an open position),
        "step" (minutes: 0-240, advance the clock; orders are only acknowledged when placed and
        fill or cancel on the next step, like on Decibel), "state" (also order_history with
        reasons, events, liquidation_price, maintenance_margin, available_margin), "market"
        (read-only, at the session clock: without market every market's mark, tick, lot, min size
        and max leverage; with market its mark, funding, rules and the book a taker order would
        meet on the next step, with priced_by and the best post-only prices that rest), "share"
        (public read-only copy; api_key shows your handle).
        Decibel's rules apply: tick and lot size, minimum size, max leverage, post-only and IOC
        violations, reduce-only trimming, cross and isolated margin, two-stage liquidation
        (margin call to 105% of maintenance, backstop below 2/3), maker 1.5 / taker 4.5 bps,
        hourly funding. Too many calls a second from one IP get Cloudflare's 1015 error: pace
        them. See pitbi.app/sandbox.
